title: Adjuster first view at /adjuster
story: REQ-15 adjuster first view with overridable AI (REQ-25)
acceptance: GET /adjuster serves the app; dev login as adjuster works
Inbox lists claims from GET adjuster inbox with severity, flag and timer-status chips

Claim view renders header, AI summary (provider/model/confidence + explain disclosure), timeline, fraud indicators, subrogation reasons, coverage summary, documents with extracted fields and confidence, regulatory timers (due/breached), next-best-action checklist, routing decision
Each fraud indicator and subrogation reason has accept/dismiss control that records a note via API (REQ-25)
node --test tests/unit/web/adjuster/*.test.mjs passes using a local fake of the adjuster view API
node --test tests/ui/adjuster.test.mjs passes (or skips cleanly without playwright): creates claim via API, opens /adjuster, logs in, sees claim summary
Does not modify files outside listed paths
brief: Build a vanilla-JS ES module app in src/web/adjuster/ (index.html, app.js, view modules, styles) reusing src/web/shared (api.js, devlogin.js, i18n.js, theme.js, tokens.css, components/). Read src/web/claimant for how a Sprint 1 app is wired and how createApp serves web folders (do not edit it); follow the same convention for the /adjuster mount. Use the adjuster inbox and adjuster claim-view endpoints as defined in architecture/contracts/modules.md; build pure render functions (data in, DOM/HTML string out) so unit tests can run with a small local fake payload matching the contract, without the server. Accept/dismiss posts a note and updates UI state optimistically with error rollback. Explain is a details/summary disclosure. Timers show due date and breached badge. Next best actions are checkboxes. Accessibility: labelled controls, landmarks, aria-live for status. Use only synthetic data. UI test: boot createApp on port 0 against a temp db with real tenants and modules, seed policies via ctx.forTenant(t).modules.coverage.seedPolicies(generatePolicies(...)) from tests/synthetic, create a claim through the public API, launch chromium via require('playwright') (createRequire from /opt/node-tools/node_modules), t.skip if import fails. Put the boot helper in tests/ui/adjuster-harness.mjs (own copy; other tickets have their own). Pitfall: other teams may not have finished adjuster endpoints; if a field is missing, render a graceful placeholder and post a contract-change request to the architecture hub. Run only your tests. Do not git commit.

verdicts.reason: All 5 criteria met; 24/24 tests pass incl. real Playwright smoke; in-scope paths only; fraud/subro decision workaround documented via contract-change request
